title: Secure Boot is disabled
description: Detects devices enrolling with Secure Boot turned off. Secure Boot is a firmware-level protection against boot-time malware and is a prerequisite for several Windows security features (VBS/Credential Guard, device health attestation) and common Intune compliance policies. Devices that support Secure Boot but have it disabled should be flagged during enrollment. Legacy BIOS devices (no Secure Boot capability) are excluded — the agent marks those with a note field when the SecureBoot registry state key is absent.
author: Autopilot Monitor

preconditions.description: Skip when the agent could not find the SecureBoot state registry key (note field set) — that indicates a legacy BIOS / non-UEFI device where Secure Boot is unsupported rather than disabled, so a warning would not be actionable.

explanation:
This device enrolled with **Secure Boot disabled**.

The firmware reports UEFI mode, but Secure Boot is turned off (`HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecureBoot\State\UEFISecureBootEnabled = 0`). Without Secure Boot the boot chain is not verified, which:

- Leaves the device exposed to bootkits and unsigned boot-time code
- Blocks or weakens Virtualization-based Security (VBS), Credential Guard and Device Health Attestation
- Typically makes the device **non-compliant** if an Intune compliance policy requires Secure Boot — Conditional Access may then block the user right after enrollment

Secure Boot is usually disabled deliberately in firmware setup (e.g. for imaging, dual-boot or legacy CSM mode) and simply never re-enabled before the device was handed to Autopilot.

remediation.title: Enable Secure Boot in UEFI firmware
steps: Reboot into the UEFI firmware setup (typically F2/F10/F12/Del during boot, or Shift+Restart -> Troubleshoot -> UEFI Firmware Settings)
Disable Legacy/CSM boot mode if it is active — Secure Boot requires native UEFI boot
Enable Secure Boot and ensure the Microsoft UEFI CA keys are selected (factory default key set)
Save, reboot and verify in Windows: msinfo32 -> 'Secure Boot State' = On, or PowerShell Confirm-SecureBootUEFI returns True
For Hyper-V test VMs: use a Generation 2 VM and enable Secure Boot in the VM's Security settings (template 'Microsoft Windows')

remediation.title: Check compliance impact
steps: Review Intune compliance policies assigned to this device for a 'Require Secure Boot' setting
If the device stays non-compliant, Conditional Access policies may block sign-in — fix firmware settings before user handover
